get_run_status:
(★free · mandatory after long-running operations) Check whether an agent is currently running for this episode. rewrite_script / extract_assets / generate_storyboards are all **minute-level** background tasks; they only return status:"generating". This tool is the only way to distinguish “still running” from “finished”.
★Typical duration (production measured): rewrite 2~4 minutes, storyboard splitting 5~10 minutes—**a single LLM call may take 3~7 minutes**. So no result within 60 seconds is completely normal, definitely not failure.
Usage: after starting, call every 30~60 seconds. running:true = still running, keep waiting, **never resend** (resending storyboard splitting replaces the entire episode’s storyboards; all tuned/generated images are lost and must be paid again); running:false = that run has ended, only then call get_storyboards / get_script to see whether artifacts were persisted.
⚠️ Service restart clears in-flight registration; runs started during restart may also show as no in-flight.
run_precheck:
(★recommended · free quality gate) Run pre-generation precheck before image/video generation to catch shots that would be rejected. Free, no credits charged. Strongly recommended before generate_frames/generate_videos to avoid wasting money on rejections.
Checks these categories: ① live-action portrait / cloned voice authorization ② high-risk image-review words ③ voiceover coverage and large gaps ④ **self-contradictory instructions (kind=prompt-conflict)**—mutually exclusive requirements within the same shot (e.g. wide shot but close-up subject marked, standing and sitting at once). No correct image can satisfy these shots; if not fixed they will be rejected repeatedly and charge repeatedly. When present, first edit the storyboard per hints, then generate images, rather than retrying.
★**You do not need to guess how to fix**: call plan_precheck_fix for platform proposals (which shot, change what to what), then apply_precheck_fix to persist (choose which items to accept; autopilot=accept all per execution mode: professional mode / unconfirmed plan / this step controlled by customer → explain to customer and only do it after customer agrees, do not decide for them; this step autopilot → do not ask customer, execute per get_production_plan autopilot.default_decisions, platform records it in get_autopilot_log)—more stable than blindly using update_shot yourself, which bypasses optimistic lock and pre-persist recheck. Some categories are not auto-fixed by system (blocked in proposals); only those require manual handling.
★★**Also come back and run this when a shot repeatedly cannot be generated**—this tool is not only a preflight check. It also reports “same-shot same-cause repeated rejection circuit-broken (repeat-reject, auto-clears in 24h)” and “frame contract contradiction”; that is exactly the answer to “why this shot never works no matter how we reroll”. **Do not blindly reroll**: while circuit break is active, every reroll repeats the same full-price rejection.
⚠️ It does **not** check whether the first frame is “before the action happens” (platform has no contract field for this yet), and does not replace get_health_report.
run_drama_precheck:
(★free · read-only) **Whole-drama** health summary: get in one call how many issues each episode has and which episodes to fix first. run_precheck is episode-level; for dozens of episodes you would need dozens of calls and manual aggregation—call this first when scanning the full drama.
Returns: episodes[] with per-episode blockers/warnings/by_kind (counts by rule code), totals for whole drama, attention[] = episodes most worth fixing first (sorted by blocker count, warning count descending).
★**How to use**: inspect attention to set priority → call run_precheck on those episodes for itemized details → use plan_precheck_fix / update_shot to fix → rerun this tool to confirm totals decreased.
⚠️ **“whole drama 0 issues” does not mean “everything was checked”**: to finish in one request, drama-level forcibly skips the only lint that needs image inspection (25s wall-clock per episode). not_covered in response lists skipped categories; to check those, run run_precheck on the corresponding episode.
⚠️ episodes[].failed=true means that episode **was not checked successfully** (not “no issues”); just retry. truncated=true means episode count exceeded limit and scan is incomplete.
plan_precheck_fix:
Let the platform **compute** how to fix "instruction self-contradiction" issues caught by run_precheck (step ①, compute only, do not modify). Billed by text usage (tiny), no quote confirmation.
★Two-step flow; this step changes no data: after receiving proposals, **explain them to the customer one by one** (which shot, change what to what, why), then pass the accepted items **unchanged** to apply_precheck_fix to persist (only the accepted items. Autopilot = accept all per execution mode: professional mode / unconfirmed plan / this step customer-controlled → explain to customer and only proceed after approval; do not decide for the customer. This step autopilot → do not ask customer; follow get_production_plan autopilot.default_decisions, and the platform records it in get_autopilot_log).
★**In professional mode, do not decide for the customer**: these rules have false positives; the platform intentionally does not offer "one-click auto-fix"—tests found nearly half the proposals in the same batch were rule false positives, and silent edits would break originally correct storyboards.
★Returned blocked lists categories the "system will not fix for you": those must be manually adjusted per run_precheck hints. Seeing blocked does not mean there is no problem; it is exactly the part that **must be handled manually**.
Omit shot_id to compute the whole episode; pass it if you only want to fix one shot.
apply_precheck_fix:
Persist proposals the customer has **confirmed** (step ②). Free (pure text DB write). Input is the proposal object returned by plan_precheck_fix; just **pass it back unchanged**—only the items the customer checked for acceptance.
★Before persisting, the platform applies three gates again: optimistic lock (if the DB value changed, skip; never overwrite others' changes), admission recheck, and self-healing gate (if the rule is not green after the edit, skip). So some items entering skipped is normal, not a failure.
★Returned remaining = how many precheck issues **remain in this episode**, not "how many fields were changed". After fixing, rerun run_precheck to confirm, then proceed to image generation.

Check before image generation; identify issues, fix first, and avoid discovering them only after the film is produced.

The platform only judges “exists / present / rejected”; “looks alike / correct / good” must be checked by you: download and open images, sample at least beginning/middle/end frames for videos, read text through with tools. Answer each checklist item (ok / issue / na; for issue, specify which item and what problem), list every inspected ref in inspected, and call submit_qc_report to submit; relay the QC conclusion to the client verbatim. If agent_qc.required=true and no report is submitted, this review_token cannot enter the next step (400 agent_qc_required); a problematic report blocks by default just like a platform error.

Check each one with your own eyes, answer it in submit_qc_report, tell the customer the result, and let the customer confirm via confirm_acceptance_criterion.

Do not decide generation failed or retry just because “it still has not appeared after waiting a while”. Do not keep spinning generate_frames, and do not send the customer to external tools to make images—external images bypass identity anchors and frame audit, so faces/costumes/style will drift.

generate_shot_frame:
After confirmation, generate or regenerate the frame for **one shot** (async). This is the proper path to fix a shot image: the platform will carry this shot’s character identity anchors, scene/prop reference images, style anchor, and frame audit; regenerated images stay consistent with the whole film. Using external tools to generate then upload bypasses this entire chain, so character/clothing/style will inevitably drift. Regeneration overwrites the shot’s existing frame image (including prior uploads) and marks this shot’s video as needing regeneration. A last frame requires this shot’s first frame to be ready (otherwise use first_frame or both first). Completion criterion: poll get_storyboards and watch this shot’s first_frame_image/last_frame_image change.

If the shot has no reopen_pair_id field (inheritance conditions not met), do not pass this parameter; use normal frame_type retry.

split_shot: Split one shot into two shots by first/last frames (structural operation). Free.
trim_shot: Trim one shot duration (in_ms/out_ms). Free; after return, call rerender_episode to reassemble the final cut.
recommend_trim_window: Trim-window action QC: for independently generated shots where declared duration < actual video duration, recommend in/out trim windows based on in-video activity detection—vendor output often has action in the second half, and trimming from 0 seconds by default can cut at a mid-action pose (e.g., hand raised but not yet struck). Free, zero charge. Not applicable to group-mode shots (group splitting is already content-aware; returns applicable=false). After receiving a recommendation, apply it with trim_shot.
scan_intra_shot_cuts: ★When the customer reports "shots cut too fast / the image jumps around inside one shot", run this first. Free, zero charge. A storyboard should be **one continuous shot**, but the vendor may hard-cut camera positions inside the video (telescope close-up → aerial wide shot → character medium shot). These cuts are invisible in the storyboard table and timeline—they can only be found by scanning frames. Returns shots_with_cuts (shot numbers with intra-shot jump cuts) / total_cuts / engine_suspect / message; shots_with_terminal_cuts separately lists suspected short abrupt tail cuts, and detail.terminal_cut gives position and status. ★Interpretation: perceived final-cut cut points = seams between shots + intra-shot cuts reported here. If this accounts for most cuts, it is not an editing pace problem; resplitting shots or changing transitions will not help. engine_suspect=true means this drama's engine is a known high-frequency source (WAN); measured WAN 11/12 shots had intra-shot cuts, Seedance 1/6, H3 0/5, and prompts cannot block it (negative constraints are already included)—first verify actual cut points and narrative intent, then decide whether to adjust splitting or regenerate; do not retry paid generation solely because of the scan warning. Ordinary intra-shot multi-cut statistics still exclude group mode and explicit montage; however, single segments after group splitting are not exempt from tail-cut checks, so still inspect shots_with_terminal_cuts/detail.terminal_cut.
scan_burned_subtitles: ★For original-voice dramas (video has built-in human speech), recommend running once before final assembly; when the customer reports "the final cut has two subtitle layers / an extra line of text in the image", run this first. Video vendors sometimes ignore "no subtitles" constraints and burn dialogue into the image—small text, usually appearing only for one or two seconds while the line is spoken. The platform final cut then overlays another subtitle layer, creating double subtitles. Reassembling cannot remove it; only regenerate_shot_video for that shot can. Samples 12 frames per shot, one vision audit, **usage-based billing** (one small vision call per shot). Returns flagged[{shot, texts, matches_dialogue, frames}] / clean / errors. matches_dialogue=true means the recognized text is this shot's dialogue, essentially confirming vendor subtitles; text naturally present in signs, book pages, screens, etc. does not count. dry_run=true reports only and does not write back; otherwise writes back, and compose_episode final-assembly precheck will list these shots as vendor_burned_text.
scan_wardrobe_consistency: ★Run this when the customer reports "the same character changed clothes / clothing color or style is wrong"; also recommended before final assembly. For each shot, compare the used first frame and one mid-video frame against each character's design image in that shot (or character sheet if none) for clothing style and color. A common cause is distant small characters being drawn by the image model in different clothes—even when reference images and prompts are correct. Overall color cast from night scenes/warm lighting does not count as inconsistency. One vision audit per shot, **usage-based billing**. Returns flagged[{shot, characters:[{name, differences}]}] / clean / errors. dry_run=true reports only and does not write back; otherwise writes back, and compose_episode final-assembly precheck will list these shots as wardrobe_mismatch. Remedy: regenerate this shot's first frame (generate_shot_frame), then regenerate_shot_video; reassembling cannot remove it.
scan_voice_consistency: ★For original-voice dramas (video has built-in human speech), run this when the customer reports "the same character's voice differs across shots / voice drifted". Free (local inference, no vendor call). For each shot with dialogue, listens to vendor-generated human speech: whether the dialogue was fully spoken, and whether the voice resembles the timbre anchor bound to that character. **Async**: returns immediately; background full-episode scan takes about 10 minutes. Only one scan per episode can run at the same time (repeat calls return started=false). By default skips shots already scanned for the current video; rescan=true rescans all. Use get_voice_consistency to check progress and per-shot results.
get_voice_consistency: Check progress and per-shot results of the voice consistency scan (started by scan_voice_consistency). Free. summary.voice_mismatch = shot numbers whose voice does not resemble the character timbre anchor (focus on these); dialogue_issues = shots where dialogue was incomplete/wrong/extra speech appeared; not_scanned_or_stale = not scanned yet or video changed and needs rescan. speaker_verdict=uncertain means the human speech is too short to judge; it is not an issue. For shots with inconsistent voice: first use get_pipeline_status native_voice_anchor to confirm the character has a bound voice, then regenerate_shot_video.
scan_dialogue_coverage: ★When the customer reports "cut before the line finished / only half the dialogue was spoken", run this first. Default **free, zero charge** (read-only access to persisted transcription audit results). Compares each original-voice shot's video audio track against the dialogue at word level, and reports conclusions by family: truncated (stops halfway through the line) / off_script (most spoken content is not the dialogue: improvising, repeating previous shot, only ambience) / extra_speech (dialogue is fully spoken but extra speech is added) / minor_gap (sporadic missing words, transcription error, ignore) / ok. ★Interpretation: the three reportable families have **different remedies**; do not simply lengthen every shot—measurements show 21% of shots with sufficient length still fail to finish the line, so "too short" is rarely the real cause (the platform already auto-raises duration by dialogue when saving storyboards). The correct fix for truncated/off_script is regenerate_shot_video (how much the vendor says is random each time; rerolling often gets the full line); if the same drama repeatedly has off_script, switch engine. ★never_audited is the most important section of this report: those shots have never been checked; "not checked" does not mean "no issue". rescan=true will run ASR comparison for them (compute-intensive, not instant; limit controls per-run cap), default does not run. TTS-dubbed shots are out of scope (TTS necessarily reads the full line; low coverage can only be transcription error). If the same episode also has "cuts too fast", that is a separate issue; run scan_intra_shot_cuts.
update_shot: Shot-by-shot edit: change a single storyboard shot's text content (shot size/action/dialogue/visual description/camera movement, etc.), facial expression (expression_hint), duration (duration), final cut speed (speed_factor), character binding (character_ids), prop binding (prop_ids; full overwrite, [] clears—use it to fix a prop missed at import instead of re-importing the whole episode; edits do not auto-regenerate frames/video), voice-over marker (character_presence), and wardrobe binding (active_wardrobe_id / appearance_wardrobes). Send only fields to change; all others stay unchanged. ★Any shot edit (accepted or rejected) invalidates unconsumed quotes covering this shot; generation then returns 409 QUOTE_INVALIDATED—edit first, read back to verify, then quote. **Free** (pure text DB write). ★Changing dialogue automatically invalidates generated TTS voice-over and subtitles for this shot (tts must be regenerated); text edits do not auto-regenerate images/video. To make visuals follow text changes, edit then regen the corresponding shot. Use get_storyboards to inspect results (each shot includes character_ids / character_bindings / scene_id / prop_ids / active_wardrobe_id / appearance_wardrobes). ★★【Change clothes here, not in text】What appears in image generation is determined by **wardrobe binding**: single-character shots use active_wardrobe_id (one outfit for the whole shot); multi-character shots use appearance_wardrobes (per character). Writing "wearing X clothes" in description/action will not change clothes. Use list_wardrobe for wardrobe id; edits do not auto-regenerate images. To update visuals, regenerate this shot's first frame then video. ★★For native-audio shots (vendor-native audio), after changing dialogue the shot video is marked "needs regeneration"—because spoken lines are **baked into the video audio**. If you final-compose without regeneration, the final cut still speaks the old line (typical symptom: dialogue seems to have moved to another shot). compose_episode lists these shots under advisory `stale_video_after_edit`; correct handling is regenerate_shot_video before final compose. ★You may also directly edit this shot's four prompt bodies (image_prompt/video_prompt/first_frame_prompt/last_frame_prompt): read current values with get_shot_prompts first; do not overwrite from scratch. @char:N / @scene:M in the body are supplemental reference markers for image generation; keep them unchanged. ★Which character sheet is injected is determined by character_ids, and background by scene_id: deleting markers will not remove already-bound people from the image. To make someone not appear, edit character_ids; if they are voice-only, set character_presence to voice_only. Conversely, do not write @char markers for unbound characters—this will inject their image. ★★【If last-frame generation is blocked, edit here】If last-frame generation reports "this shot is marked as a state change, but nowhere describes what it looks like at the end" (TERMINAL_DESC_GATE), fix by writing **what the final image should look like** into this shot's last_frame_prompt, then regenerate the last frame. Do not retry image generation—shots of this type (action_motion_class=state_change without terminal state) historically succeed at 9.4%, versus 40.2% with terminal-state description; without adding the description, the vendor prompt has no terminal-state section, so it still draws the same as the first frame, is rejected again, and each regeneration still charges normally. terminal_desc_missing=true from get_shot_prompts is this signal.

The contract itself is internal: cannot be read or edited directly. This tool only returns outcome: updated (changed and effective) / unchanged (derived result same as current) / rejected (derived result self-contradictory, not adopted, original contract kept) / no_candidate (no usable result, original contract kept) / stale (shot changed during derivation, result not written; call again after edits), plus note for next step. Insufficient credits returns 402. ★When to use: image generation/precheck/review repeatedly says the number of people is wrong, or a partial shot (hand/prop close-up) is treated as a full-person shot in generation or review, and you have already edited text or bindings—the autofiller only fills blanks and does not overwrite existing contracts; without this tool, edits will not enter the contract. ★Correct order: first update_shot to make the image text correct (who is visible, who is voice-only via character_presence voice_only, unbind anyone who should not appear from character_ids), then call this tool; calling without text edits usually returns unchanged. ★One text AI call, postpaid by token (same chain as autofill_storyboards); inform the customer before calling. ★Only changes this one contract field; does not touch dialogue/prompts/other specialized fields. Generated first/last frames are not auto-regenerated; to update visuals, regenerate frames for this shot (quote first). ★updated invalidates unconsumed frame/video quotes for this shot and the same episode; quote again afterward.

Writing a marker for an unbound character will inject that character's image. ★This is the body layer in the storyboard sheet; during image/video generation the platform also appends identity anchors, consistency constraints, and reference-image instructions (not here, and you do not need to write them). replace_shot_dialogue:

Follow the returned alternatives (regenerate this shot's video / targeted edit / replace audio only—the last option does not change mouth motion).

★Receiving **503 code=lipsync.unavailable** = the platform currently has no available lip-sync service; this request was not submitted and no fee was deducted; retrying is useless. Follow the returned alternatives (regenerate this shot's video / targeted edit / replace audio only—the last option does not change mouth motion).

generate_effects: Automatically match visual effects for the full episode. Backend async, postpaid by usage.

clone_voice: Clone voice timbre from an **authorized** audio sample, returns voice_id. **No character or drama required first**. ⚠️ Sample must be a voice **authorized with consent** by the person/rights holder (otherwise infringement, same as real-person/copyright issues). Charged at platform price (flat price per voice). After cloning, directly use speak_with_voice to audition/download; only when using it to dub a final cut do you then need set_character_voice to bind it to a character.
speak_with_voice: Make a voice speak arbitrary text and return a downloadable audio URL. **No character or episode required**—after cloning, use this to verify whether the voice matches, or use the audio elsewhere directly. Charged by text length (tts tier).
list_voices: List available voices: my cloned private voices + platform public voices (voice_id/name/audition sample). Free.
delete_voice: Delete a cloned voice from my voice library (platform public voices cannot be deleted). Free.
design_voice:
**When there is no voice sample**, create a new voice from a one-sentence description (e.g. a dedicated voice for narration or a character). After submission, candidates are generated in the background (about 1~3 minutes). Poll with get_voice_design and audition them, then choose one and save it to the voice library with save_designed_voice. **Generation is free** (1 concurrent task per person, 30 times per 24 hours); saving charges the same as voice cloning.
★Describing “what you want” works better than “what you do not want”: age, gender, timbre (deep/clear/hoarse/breathy), speaking speed, emotion.
★You must choose and fix one voice before dubbing: the same description generates a different person each time. Only after fixing a sample and cloning it will the whole episode use the same voice. Therefore there is no tool to “dub the whole episode directly from a description”; this is intentional.
★Do not use real person/celebrity names in the description to imitate a specific person’s voice (same authorization red line as voice cloning).
get_voice_design: Check progress of a design_voice task. After status=done, download each candidate to a local wav (returns local_path) and provide it to the client for audition and selection; when queued/waiting_memory/running, check again after a dozen seconds. Free. Candidates are retained for 6 hours.
save_designed_voice: Save the candidate selected by the client into the voice library and return voice_id (like lib:12). **Charged the same as voice cloning** (saving the same candidate repeatedly does not charge again). Then bind it to a character with set_character_voice (narrator is also a character) before using it for dubbing; you can also use speak_with_voice first to audition more sentences.
set_character_voice:
Bind a voice to a character; later generate_tts will use it to dub that character. Free. This is only needed when producing video—cloning and auditioning do not require a character.
★★【In native-audio dramas (use_clip_audio=true, default), this step is “voice locking”】When the bound voice is **the client’s own authorized voice** (cloned by clone_voice / uploaded by the client, not a public voice), later video generation will pass this audio directly to the video vendor as reference audio. The vendor will speak according to it, and lip sync is naturally aligned—otherwise each group/single shot samples the voice independently, so the same character’s voice may drift across shots. Public voices are only used for TTS dubbing and will not be passed to the vendor.
★Cost: shots where this character appears will no longer feed a character-sheet video anchor during video generation (the reference video’s audio track overrides reference audio; only one can be used). Character identity must instead be carried by the character sheet/reference images—so confirm the character sheet and reference images are ready before binding.
★Only affects videos generated **after binding**: bind first, then generate_videos. For videos already generated, the cheapest way to unify the voice is repair_episode_dialogue (only_flagged=false, re-dub full lines with the cloned voice, do not regenerate video, charged at the TTS tier); regenerate_shot_video also works but is orders of magnitude more expensive.
★After binding, assign_voices will no longer overwrite this character (the client’s own voice has highest priority).
set_voice_anchor_from_shot:
Select a character’s voice line (voice baseline) from a shot in this episode. Free. No external audio source is required from the client—use the voice this character has already spoken in the video.
★★【In native-audio dramas (use_clip_audio=true, default), this is “voice locking”】After selection, later video generation will pass this audio to the video vendor as reference audio, so the same character’s voice across shots follows it; without locking, the vendor samples each shot independently and the voice may drift across shots.
★Which shot to choose: a shot where the character **speaks alone, has a longer line, and has no background music or interruptions by others**; start_s/dur_s can clip only part of it (if omitted, the default window is used, and duration is automatically clamped to each engine’s limit).
★Only affects videos generated **afterward**. Shots already generated before locking will appear in get_pipeline_status under native_voice_anchor.stale_shots; regenerate them with regenerate_shot_video to unify the voice. The cheapest workflow is: generate one shot for each speaking character first, select the voice line, then batch-generate the remaining shots.
★Works even if the dialogue field is empty: actual audio is authoritative—the platform uses calibrated voice activity detection to confirm there is speech in the selected interval, and uses the transcription text as anchor text; if no speech is detected or no usable text can be transcribed, it rejects (a wrong anchor would pollute all later shots’ voices, so reject rather than guess). The response field text_source indicates whether text came from dialogue or transcription.
★Preview first with preview:true: only clips and returns preview_url plus anchor text, **without writing to the character**; if it sounds right, remove preview and formally submit with the same start_s/dur_s.
★Noise removal and acceptance check (effective when enabled by the platform for the episode; response contains hygiene): automatically removes pure environmental-noise pauses between two lines and measures sample noise floor (noise_floor_before/after, threshold threshold). In preview, preview_url is the **cleaned** sample and raw_preview_url is the original—**ask the client to compare both before/after by listening**. verdict=fail means obvious environmental noise or music is under the voice (removing pauses cannot fix it; cloning and the video vendor will learn it as part of the timbre), and formal submission will be rejected: choose a cleaner shot, or adjust start_s/dur_s to avoid background sound; only pass allow_issues:true to write it if the client has listened and explicitly insists.
★If the client has an authorized external audio source, use clone_voice + set_character_voice instead; choose one of the two, and the later setting overrides the earlier one.
export_handoff_pack:
After delivery traceability is enabled, an immutable export manifest is saved (assets are not modified). Keep pack_id and manifest_sha256, and reference them when returning an external final cut. Export the “asset handoff package” manifest for this episode: downloadable URLs for each-shot raw clips + dialogue tracks + sound effects + music + subtitles, for you to complete transition decisions, stitching, mixing, and subtitle burn-in **on your own side**—the platform does not participate in final assembly. Free, zero credits.
★Local color grading / third-party AI post: purpose=local_color; when there are only images, pass media_type=images, no need to generate video. This mode preserves source files, disables the export package’s automatic LUT, and includes post-production notes and a local comparison-page flow; it does not upload to third parties, charge for generation, or backfill the platform. Image sources may already have been processed, so not all exported images can be promised as ungraded originals.

【Recommended workflow】① Call this tool to get manifest; ② Download raw clips locally via clips[].url; ③ Watch the clips yourself and decide which transition to use at each seam (manifest provides scene_boundary as a scene-boundary criterion), write a plan.json; ④ Use get_handoff_toolchain to get compile_timeline.py to expand the timeline and assemble.sh to assemble the final cut. The toolchain already calculates how subtitles/dialogue/SFX shift after overlapping transitions are added.

【Three facts that will break things if ignored】
① **Where the voice is must be read per shot from `shots[].voice_track.location`, not from the episode-level audio_contract.mode**—the latter is an episode-level declaration, while in all-offscreen-narration shots the narration is mixed into the raw clip on the platform completion side, so it can differ per shot within the same episode. The four values require different handling: `separate_file`=dialogue is in dialogue_audio; if you do not lay it in, this shot has no lines; `baked_in_clip`=already in the raw clip audio track; overlaying it again causes double voice; `missing`=**platform side confirmed missing** (narration compensation failed); subtitles still exist but the sound is nowhere—regenerate this shot on the platform; extending a transition cannot hide it; `unknown`=there are lines but the source cannot be found, **you must listen to the raw clip** before deciding. ★Subtitles never imply there is sound: subtitles are per sentence, audio is per shot. For shots with `conflicts_with_contract=true`, trust measurement; notes already name them by shot number.
② Each shot must be trimmed using trim_head_ms / duration_ms before use; directly stitching the full raw clip will include head/tail deformed frames that the platform already QC’d out. ★From manifest_version=0.2 the in/out points are projected from the platform's final-cut timeline (the same as build_av_timing_contract and the platform cut), and clip.url is the file that timeline actually uses (clip.source_kind); in 0.1 the pack computed its own trim, which did not match the platform cut. speed_factor≠1 must be retimed by that factor and freeze_pad_ms>0 must be filled by cloning the last frame (duration_ms=(out_ms−in_ms)/speed_factor+freeze_pad_ms), or the total length will not match; subtitles_burned_in=true means do not burn subtitles again, color_graded=true means do not apply the LUT again; shots with trim_basis≠platform_timeline are untrimmed, and notes say why. An old toolchain copy that only accepts 0.1 will reject 0.2 — run save_handoff_toolchain again.
③ Subtitle cues, dialogue_audio.offset_ms, and sfx[].offset_ms are all based on “millisecond 0 after this shot’s trim”, not absolute final-cut time. No matter how many overlapping transitions you add, do not modify them—let compile_timeline.py expand them; do not manually accumulate times.

Before you assemble, run build_av_timing_contract → get_av_timing_contract (free): per shot the measured source length, the platform final cut's in/out points, transition overlap and freeze padding, and whether the voice is already mixed into the clip or on a separate track — check your timeline's total against it.

If you want the platform to assemble it, or need platform-level quality gates (final assembly precheck / equal audio-video duration / loudness mastering), use compose_episode.
get_handoff_toolchain:
Get the source code for the asset handoff package assembly toolchain (compile_timeline.py timeline compiler / assemble.sh ffmpeg assembly script). Free. This tool only returns source text and **will not** write files on your machine—save it to your working directory yourself before running.
compile_timeline.py expands “shot-relative” subtitle/dialogue/SFX anchors into absolute timecodes on your own timeline and handles global offsets caused by overlapping transitions; assemble.sh is a complete ffmpeg assembly baseline from raw clips to final cut (trim → normalize → concat/xfade → music sidechain → subtitles → two-pass master). Dependencies: ffmpeg (with libass for subtitle burn-in), ffprobe, jq, python3.
save_handoff_toolchain:
Write the assembly toolchain (fetch_pack.py / compile_timeline.py / assemble.sh) directly to a local directory, avoiding manual copy/paste. Free. The directory must **already exist** and be an absolute path; filenames are fixed and cannot be customized.
Refuses to write into hidden directories (~/.ssh, ~/.config, .git…) and system directories—this is disk writing, not reading, and overwriting the wrong place is irreversible.
Full workflow after writing to disk:
  python3 fetch_pack.py manifest.json -o ./pack   # Download assets and materialize inline subtitles as SRT
  python3 compile_timeline.py ./pack [--transitions plan.json]
  ./assemble.sh ./pack out.mp4 [plan.json]
get_post_production_checklist: Read this episode's **post-production effects checklist** (free). Items marked in the script as [VFX: …] or written in shot prompts as "post-production / composited later" are **not composited by the platform**—image and video generation leave them out and the final cut does not add them, so the finished episode lacks these story elements unless handled. Per item: shot_number, time start_s~end_s, content, source (vfx_tag shot annotation / prompt / script_unassigned = in the rewritten script but not attached to any shot), narrative_required (story-critical; cosmetic items such as color grading are false), status (pending / done_external / waived). ★Review before composing; tell the client about narrative_required pending items and ask: do it in external post (then mark_post_production_item done_external), change the shot so the platform draws it (update_shot then regenerate that shot), or drop it (waived). review_videos / compose_episode give an advisory for unhandled items.
mark_post_production_item: Mark one item of the post-production checklist (free): status=done_external (client finished it outside the platform) / waived (client decided not to do it) / pending (undo). key comes from get_post_production_checklist; it changes after the shot or prompt is edited—on 400, re-read the checklist. (Marking post-production items requires explicit client consent in every execution mode, including autopilot.) Marking is bookkeeping only and does not change the final cut; if the client wants the externally finished version delivered, use register_external_delivery.
get_drama_logo: Read this drama's final-cut logo settings (image URL / width / corner / margins / opacity). Free. null = no logo set.
set_drama_logo: Set an image logo (corner bug) for this drama's final cut; it is overlaid above subtitles for the whole video. Free, no video regeneration. Upload the logo first with upload_image (transparent PNG recommended) and pass its URL as src. Size/margins are in px on a 720p-height baseline and scale with the output height (e.g. ~260px wide on 1080x1920 portrait -> width≈98). Takes effect on the next compose_episode / rerender_episode. Pass logo:null to clear.
get_acceptance_criteria: Read this episode's **customer acceptance items** (free): specific requirements the customer set for a shot or the whole episode. Each item keeps three separate states — auto_review (platform automatic review, per stage; not_covered = the platform has no check for this category, no_related_finding does NOT mean the requirement is met), agent_qc (your per-item conclusion from submit_qc_report, per stage), and client (the customer's own confirmation). ★Passing the platform review or your generic QC does not mean the customer's specific requirements pass — walk the customer through these items before delivery. orphan=true means the bound shot was deleted.
add_acceptance_criteria: Register customer acceptance items (free): when the customer states a **specific requirement** for a shot or the whole episode (identity, wardrobe, prop color, lip sync, visual artifacts, etc.), record it in the customer's own words. review_frames / review_videos will then append it to agent_qc.checklist (ids start with req:) for you to check item by item, and the result is recorded separately. ★One requirement per item; for a shot use shot_number (current shot number) or storyboard_id, omit both for the whole episode. Registering invalidates review_tokens already issued for that stage — re-review. ★Only register what the customer actually said; never invent requirements.
update_acceptance_criterion: Edit a customer acceptance item (free). Changing the text / category / shot / stages resets all three states of that item (the requirement changed, old conclusions no longer count); re-run the review to check it. To delete, use delete_acceptance_criterion. item_id comes from get_acceptance_criteria. (Editing customer acceptance items requires explicit client consent in every execution mode, including autopilot.)
confirm_acceptance_criterion: Record the **customer's own** confirmation of an acceptance item (free): accepted / rejected / pending (undo). Only the client state is written; the platform auto review and your QC conclusion are untouched. ★Call it only after the customer has explicitly stated their decision, with confirm_client_statement:true; you must never confirm on the customer's behalf, autopilot included.
delete_acceptance_criterion: Delete a customer acceptance item (free; its three states go with it). item_id comes from get_acceptance_criteria. (Deleting customer acceptance items requires explicit client consent in every execution mode, including autopilot.)
quote_local_frame_edit: Quote: how many credits a **local edit of one frame of one shot** costs (fix a face, close a mouth, clean halo edges, remove a stray object). Zero cost. Use it when the customer only wants a small part of the image changed — do not edit it in an outside image tool and upload_shot_frame it back: outside tools also change details the customer already approved, bypass the identity anchors and audits, and break the provenance chain. To redraw the whole frame use quote_shot_frame / generate_shot_frame. The platform pastes the edited area back onto the original through a feathered mask: pixels outside the boxes stay unchanged. ★Billing: each candidate is charged as one image (unit_points × candidates; the image count is fixed, so estimated_points is the actual charge and equals typical_points). **Candidates rejected by the platform checks (visible seam, edit not applied, identity audit failed) are never refunded** — tell the customer this together with the points. Vendor failures are refunded automatically. ★Rolled out per drama and per edit_kind; otherwise 403 LOCAL_FRAME_EDIT_UNAVAILABLE, whose open_kinds lists the kinds open to every drama (e.g. object_remove) — for any other kind fall back to generate_shot_frame. Face edits without character_id → 400 CHARACTER_REQUIRED; face edits do not send the character portrait (only the cropped base), after pasting back the face is compared against the original to check it is still the same person (a clear mismatch is rejected, an uncertain one is left for a human; both are charged as usual).
local_frame_edit: After confirmation, **locally edit one frame of one shot** (async, charged). Parameters must equal the quote_local_frame_edit call exactly (any change to regions / instruction / kind / character / candidates / base image → 409 QUOTE_PARAMS_CHANGED; re-quote for free). Returns edit_id; poll with get_local_frame_edit. ★**It never replaces the current frame automatically**: show the candidates (composited_url) to the customer first; only adopt_local_frame_edit writes the chosen one into the shot and marks the shot video as needing regeneration. ★Rejected candidates are charged and not refunded. Requires the review_storyboards review_token (and asset_review_token on rollout dramas), same as generate_shot_frame.
get_local_frame_edit: Check progress and results of a local frame edit (free). status=running → keep waiting; when completed, look at each candidate: composited_url (the result pasted back onto the original — show this to the customer), verdict (pass = usable; warn = usable but needs a human look — REGION_SEAM_WARN possible seam / EDIT_NOT_APPLIED barely changed / IDENTITY_NEEDS_REVIEW face-comparison score in the grey zone, not auto-approved / IDENTITY_NOT_JUDGEABLE side view, looking down or face too small to judge / IDENTITY_COMPARE_LOW legacy identity score low / IDENTITY_AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE identity not audited; reject = not recommended — REGION_MISALIGNED misaligned paste / IDENTITY_MISMATCH face comparison says it became a different person / IDENTITY_AUDIT_REJECTED frame audit failed, possibly a composition issue already present in the original frame), reason_text (a plain-language explanation of each reason — relay it to the customer as is), metrics, identity_audit, identity_compare (face edits: with method=face_embedding the decision uses face embeddings — similarity to the same face before the edit ≥0.75 passes, <0.60 is a mismatch, in between goes to a human; vlm_reference is recorded only. Without a method field it is the legacy advisory score). ★Still check face edits with your own eyes — the platform cannot judge side views, downward-looking or small faces. Download and look at composited_url yourself, tell the customer, then adopt_local_frame_edit the one they pick. Rejected candidates are not refunded (including those failing the frame audit because of an issue already in the original frame).
adopt_local_frame_edit: Adopt a local-edit candidate as this shot's current frame (free). Same follow-up as an uploaded frame: the shot video is marked for regeneration and adjacent seams are repaired. ★Only after the customer has looked and chosen. If the frame changed after the edit → 409 BASE_FRAME_CHANGED (start a new edit on the current frame); verdict=reject candidates are refused by default (409 CANDIDATE_REJECTED) — pass accept_rejected:true only when the customer insists after seeing it.
audit_seam_directions: Pre-video seam direction check (advisory, never blocks any step): for every pair of adjacent shots, compares "previous shot's last frame (or first frame if none) ↔ this shot's first frame" for the same subject jumping left/right sides of the frame (a reversed eyeline is noted with it), reversed motion direction, and shot-size jumps (same subject, extreme long ↔ close-up). Eyeline alone and key-light direction are observed but not reported: production replay showed too many false positives on those (better to miss than to nag). Shots that look fine alone but jump when cut together usually fail on these. Complements audit_seams, which checks identity/wardrobe/props/object state but not direction or position. ★When: after first frames (and needed last frames) are done and chain_frames has run, before review_frames / generate_videos. Scene changes, declared jump cuts, insert shots and title/black cards are skipped automatically. ★dry_run first (default, free): returns the seams to observe plus estimated_points (upper bound) and typical_points (usual cost); tell the client both — billed by actual text tokens. After the client agrees, pass dry_run=false + confirm_usage_billing=true. Execution is asynchronous and returns immediately; read results with get_seam_directions a minute or two later. Seams already observed with unchanged frames are not billed again.
get_seam_directions: (Free) Read audit_seam_directions results: each issue gives the seam shot numbers, the problem (subject jumps sides, reversed motion, shot-size jump) and fixes (chain_shot_from mode=reframe to regenerate this shot's first frame anchored on the previous last frame / update_shot to state facing then generate_shot_frame / align_prev_shot when the previous shot already has video / split_shot to insert an intermediate shot size). Results are advisory: explain them to the client and let the client pick which to fix; intentional reverse shots, turns or impact cuts can be ignored. not_audited>0 = seams not observed yet or frames changed since; running=true = still running. review_frames' seam_direction_advisory is a summary of the same results. This tool only looks at pre-video still frames; after videos are generated, check seams with preview_seams (free short-clip previews).
get_shot_verse_cards: Read this shot's current poem/lyric text cards (free). set_shot_verse_cards is a **full overwrite**—read before editing. enabled=false means the drama is not enabled yet (saved cards will not appear in the cut).
set_shot_verse_cards: Add/change/clear poem & lyric text cards on one shot (burned into the final cut; free, data only). Up to 6 cards per shot, **full overwrite** (read with get_shot_verse_cards first); cards=[] clears. Covers three staples of cinematic period-style shorts: (1) vertical or horizontal poem/lyric lines fading in at the left, right or center (a newline in text starts a new column/line, punctuation is kept; stagger several cards with start_ms); (2) a full-screen black closing card with backdrop="black" (usually on the last shot, orient=horizontal, position=center); (3) end credits over the picture with motion="scroll_up" (scrolls bottom to top, one name per line, blank lines separate groups). Cards automatically stay out of the dialogue-subtitle band, so they never overlap spoken subtitles; oversized text is shrunk instead of overflowing. Run compose_episode afterwards to re-cut (rerender_episode reuses the saved timeline and will not pick it up). enabled=false from get_shot_verse_cards means the drama is not enabled yet. ★Do not download the video, overlay text yourself and re-upload—that bypasses renderer fonts and subtitle avoidance. ★Only use the poem/credits text the customer supplied; do not invent it.
get_theme_songs: Read an episode's theme-song settings (free). set_theme_songs is a **full overwrite**—read before editing. enabled=false means the drama is not enabled yet.
set_theme_songs: Attach/change/clear **theme songs with vocals** on an episode (opening song, ending song, or an insert song over a range of shots; free, data only, full overwrite, songs=[] clears; up to 3 per episode). Song source, pick one: (1) the customer's own song—upload via upload-url (kind=audio) and pass the public_url as audio_url; (2) platform-composed or library track—pass track_id; (3) an existing https URL. placement: opening = from 0 until the song ends or shot sb_to ends / ending = pinned to the end, or starting at shot sb_from / range = shots sb_from..sb_to (both required). Vocals never fight dialogue: with instrumental_url (the same song's backing track) the default dialogue_mode=instrumental fades the vocal out and the backing track in while someone speaks, then swaps back; with only the full song, dialogue_mode=duck lowers the whole song by duck_db (default -18 dB) during speech. Background music automatically yields inside the theme-song range (bgm_yield, default true) and is unchanged elsewhere. gain_db defaults to -8; track_offset_ms skips an intro. Run compose_episode afterwards; enabled=false means the drama is not enabled yet. ★Do not download the cut, remix it yourself and re-upload.
